South Africans stranded abroad

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
COVID -19 has stranded hundreds of South Africans abroad. How do they come home?

Unique Selling Point:
COVID-19 has stranded hundreds of South Africans abroad. Many of them are on-board the cruise ships Costa Luminosa & Costa Pacifica and are still at sea because they have been refused permission to dock at European ports in Spain, France & Italy. What is to become of them? When will they be allowed to disembark? Most importantly, with a travel restrictions in place, how will they get home?

Press Release:


How will more than 1500 South Africans make their way home after COVID-19 lockdowns have stranded them in various countries around the world? With flights suspended and global travel restrictions in place, many travellers face uncertainty as they try to stay safe and comfortable on foreign soil.

Script:


SCRIPT
V/O Montage
Covid-19 has turned the world upside down

and international travel into a mine field

It has transformed dream holidays into nightmares

Leaving thousands trapped

And increasingly desperate


OPENING LINK: The COVID-19 pandemic continues to play havoc on our daily lives. As countries shut their borders and close their airports to contain the spread of the virus, over 1000 South Africans have been left stranded in various countries around the world and unsure of how they will get home.




V/O: With South Africa in a state of total lockdown till at least the 16 April, SA citizens trapped abroad have been left with no way to return home. Many of these marooned travelers have set up a facebook group called “Home Away from Home” and DA MP Darren Bergman is making representations on their behalf.

Darren gives a few examples of the situation that many South Africans find themselves in

V/O: There are around 1500 SA citizens in far flung countries all around the world. From the UK to Europe, The Americas to Africa, Asia, Australia and the Middle East.

Darren on how he’s been trying to assist them


LINK: Many of the South Africans stranded abroad are tourists. With OR Tambo shut down right now, many local travel agencies are doing their best to get affected passengers home safely

V/O: This is no easy task as MD of Flight Centre Andrew Stark explains

Andrew on how they’ve been trying to assist customers who were abroad.

LUMINOSA LINK: With our country in a state of total lockdown, millions of South Africans are confined to their homes. It’s one thing being stuck in your house but imagine being trapped on a cruise-liner infected with COVID-19. That’s what faced dozens of South Africans on-board the Costa Luminosa all needing answers to a desperate question: How will I get home?

V/O: Robyn Terbrugge’s parents were part of a contingent of 40 South Africans aboard the Luminosa.

Comment from Robyn about her parents holiday which was turned upside down when a passenger tested positive for COVID-19

V/O: Randall Carr’s parents were also on-board. He doesn’t understand why the Captain decided to make the transatlantic crossing to Europe knowing that COVID-19 had infected the ship.

We can also make use of Randall’s comments too.

V/O: With the Luminosa heading to Europe, passengers were confined to their cabins. Eventually, the ship docked at the French port of Marseilles on the 18th of March.

Comment from Randall: 85 sick passengers on board

V/O: Only Americans, Canadians & Germans were allowed to leave. The remaining passengers were forced to stay on the ship as it set sail for the Italian port of Savona

V/O: Relieved to be back on dry land, the South Africans had to endure a 9-hour bus journey where they were taken to a hotel in Rome to begin a 14 day quarantine period.

With their internet access restored, Carte Blanche has been able to speak to some of the passengers like Ruth Freemantle

Comments from Ben & Desiree about their ordeal

V/O: They may be off the ship, but life hasn’t become easier. They are confined to their hotel rooms with little to no physical contact with the outside world as Ben and Desiree Haarmse
explain

They must talk about life in the hotel and then cover the fact that they don’t know when they’re coming home or how that will happen

We need to find a comment about how they feel let down and abandoned by Costa Cruises

COSTA LINK: We’ve reached out to Costa Cruises for comment. We’ve emailed them, tried to call them but haven’t yet had a reply.
V/O: It’s been hazardous to be on-board a cruise ship in a time of COVID-19. Several are still stuck at sea trying desperately to find safe harbour. But at least there have been some good news stories.

Gerry Norris was one of 168 South Africans on-board the Costa Pacifica. Thankfully they were allowed to dock in Rome last Monday.

Comment from Gerry about his trip and his relief in being at home in Cape Town.

V/O: In spite of the dangers of Covid-19, some cruise ships have continued to operate. The MSC Orchestra left Durban on Monday 16 March, the day after President Ramaphosa banned all non-essential travel.

Anisia Du Plessis was one of 2500 South Africans on-board

Comment from Anisia about why she decided to go through with the trip

V/O: MD of MSC Cruises Ross Volk defended the decision to embark on the trip

Comment from Ross Volk

V/O: In spite of precautions taken by MSC Cruises, it has now been confirmed that one of the passengers on board from the 13th- the 16th March has tested positive.

Comment from Ross & Anisia about the COVID+ test result




V/O: If you were on the MSC orchestra at any time from the 28th Feb to the 20th March, you may need to be tested. Please contact the Department of Health in KwaZulu Natal or the Free State.

V/O: Back in Rome, the South Africans in quarantine learnt this past weekend that 2 of them have also tested positive.

Comment from Desiree about the COVID+ South Africans and what it’s done to her state of mind

V/O: Desiree’s desperation is shared by all South Africans trapped abroad. Thankfully the government has heard their call for help…

President Ramaphosa Clip: “We know that there are many South Africans who are currently abroad and want to come home.

We are paying attention to this and will be giving assistance where possible within our constrained resources.”


V/O: Following the President’s address, the next day It was announced at an inter-ministerial briefing that travel restrictions will be relaxed to allow for the repatriation of South African citizens.

Minister Naledi Pandor said “priority would be given to those who were stranded at airports, running out of accommodation, and the elderly and the sick.

Through their Whatsapp group Carte Blanche has learnt that the South Africans have been told by Costa that their costs will be covered while they are abroad.

They will also assist with chartering a flight to South Africa.

Finally after weeks of stress and uncertainty, there is a way home…

Final Comment from Desiree crying about just wanting to come home.
